To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nephritogenic IgG in IgAN-prone mice is rapidly deposited in a focal and subendothelium manner in the glomeruli.
nephritogenic IgAs from IgA nephritis (IgAN)-prone mice have strong affinity to the glomerulus and deposit along the capillary, and that these deposits disappear within 24 h.
IgA from nephropathy-proned mice has strong affinity to glomerular lesions, and the deposits disappear 24-h after a single IgA injection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new hypothesis that IgA nephropathic IgA is deposited in a focal and/or segmental manner along the glomeruli and that the glomerular cellular activation may be induced by IgA deposits.
the kinetics of glomerular deposition of nephritogenic IgAs in IgAN-prone mice.
the precise events of IgA deposition in IgAN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glomerular deposition of nephritogenic IgAs is not limited to the mesangium and is a dynamic process.
glomerular deposition of nephritogenic IgAs is a dynamic process and the glomerular lesions may be expressed under a balance between IgA deposition and clearance.
the mesangial deposits of nephritogenic IgAs may not induce hematuria but may be a consequence of the disease process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deposition of IgA nephritogenic IgG in susceptible mice is a focal and segmentally distributed event along the glomerulus.
IgA from IgAN patients is nephritogenic and induces acute glomerular injury, and that the glomerular lesions in IgAN are not only mesangial but focal and segmental.
the mesangial IgG deposition in IgAN is a secondary process, and that the focal and segmental IgA deposition in IgAN may play an important role in the pathogenesis of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glomerular injury in IgAN may not be induced by IgA deposits in mesangial areas.
the deposition of IgA is a focal and segmentally dynamic event, which is consistent with the clinical observation that the intensity of IgA deposition does not correlate with the degree of injury.
IgA deposition in the mesangium is not the only mechanism that causes IgA nephropathic lesions, and that the glomerular deposition of IgA is not static but dynamic.
